dedupe_keys.name: critical infrastructure spatial index cisi and global harmonised critical infrastructure dataset

description: This dataset is a first globally harmonised spatial representation of critical infrastructure, produced by Nirandjan, Koks, Ward and colleagues at the Institute for Environmental Studies of Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam with the University of Oxford and described in Scientific Data 9, 150 (2022). It aggregates OpenStreetMap features of 39 critical infrastructure types grouped into seven overarching systems and rasterises them into two products: the amount of infrastructure per type in each grid cell, and the Critical Infrastructure Spatial Index (CISI), a composite measure of the spatial intensity of infrastructure. Both are provided at 0.10 and 0.25 degree resolution as two zip archives (194.4 MB in total) in version 1.0.0 of 15 June 2021 on Zenodo, under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence and free of charge. The authors propose it for exploring the global landscape of infrastructure, identifying hotspots and as exposure input to large-scale risk assessments. Caveats: it inherits OpenStreetMap's uneven completeness, especially in low-income regions, reflects a single snapshot, and the grid aggregation removes network connectivity. It serves hazard exposure and multi-hazard resilience screening and climate adaptation studies, and is related to the GIRI risk model and the open-gira workflow catalogued here.
